mcqs.question: A flex container has `flex-direction: column`. Which axis does `justify-content` now control?
options: The vertical axis, because column always means vertical alignment properties swap in
Whichever axis is the main axis — vertical here, since column makes the main axis run top to bottom
It still controls the horizontal axis regardless of flex-direction
justify-content has no effect once flex-direction is set to column
mcqs.explanation: justify-content always targets the main axis, and flex-direction is what defines which physical direction the main axis points in — column rotates it to vertical. The first option sounds right but reverses cause and effect: it isn't a special-cased swap, it's the same rule applied to a different axis.

mcqs.question: A flex row has `flex-wrap: wrap` and ends up with three lines of items. You want to add vertical space between those three lines. Which property does that?
options: align-content, because it spaces multiple lines apart on the cross axis
align-items, because it controls cross-axis positioning
justify-content, because line spacing is a main-axis concern
gap, since it is the only property that adds space anywhere in flexbox
mcqs.explanation: align-content operates on whole lines when wrapping produces more than one; align-items only repositions items within a single line, which is why it appears to do nothing when there's just one line. gap can also add space between lines, but align-content is the alignment property purpose-built for that job and the one being tested here.

mcqs.question: Three flex items share `flex: 1` except one, which is `flex: 2`. The container has 300px of extra space beyond every item's basis. How is that extra space divided?
options: Equally — flex-grow only matters when values are unequal by more than double
200/50/50, because flex: 2 always claims exactly two-thirds of the total container width
150/75/75, split by the grow ratio 2:1:1 across the extra space only
The item with flex: 2 takes all 300px since it has the higher grow value
mcqs.explanation: flex-grow distributes only the leftover space after each item's basis is honored, in proportion to the grow values — 2:1:1 across four shares of the 300px extra gives 150/75/75. It isn't a fixed two-thirds of the whole width, and a higher grow value doesn't mean winner-take-all.

mcqs.question: Why does giving `.main-content { flex: 1; }` inside a column-direction flex body produce a sticky footer, without any absolute positioning?
options: flex: 1 sets a fixed height equal to 100vh minus the header and footer
The main content absorbs all leftover vertical space after siblings take their basis, pushing whatever comes after it to the bottom of the flex container
flex: 1 automatically applies position: sticky to the element
It only works if the footer itself also has flex: 1
mcqs.explanation: flex: 1 makes that item grow to consume the container's remaining space, so with a min-height: 100vh body the footer is naturally pushed to the bottom edge on short pages. There's no implicit position change and no requirement that the footer share the same flex value.

mcqs.question: A flex item has `flex-shrink: 1` but a long unbreakable string still overflows its container instead of shrinking. What's the most likely cause?
options: flex-shrink was set to a decimal value that browsers round down to 0
The parent is missing flex-wrap: wrap
flex-shrink only works inside flex-direction: column containers
The item's implicit min-width: auto is holding it at its content size, and flex-shrink can't shrink it past that floor
mcqs.explanation: Flex items default to min-width: auto, an implicit floor equal to their content's minimum size, and shrink never overrides that floor — only an explicit min-width: 0 does. flex-wrap controls whether items move to new lines, which is unrelated to a single item refusing to shrink.

mcqs.question: In a navbar built with flexbox, the action buttons on the right must never get visually squeezed even when the search box grows. Which property on the actions container achieves that?
options: flex-shrink: 0, so the actions never give up space to the search box
flex-grow: 0, since grow is what prevents shrinking under pressure
min-width: auto, to force the browser to protect its size
justify-content: flex-end, to push it away from the shrinking element
mcqs.explanation: flex-shrink: 0 explicitly opts an item out of the shrink calculation entirely, so it holds its size no matter how tight the container gets. flex-grow: 0 only stops it from taking extra space, it says nothing about giving space up under a squeeze, and min-width: auto is already the default, not an opt-in fix.
